chunks: 1463 - Al-Ḥalabī narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about the woman: is she to perform ghusl (ritual bath) on the day of Jumuʿah, al-Fiṭr, al-Aḍḥā, and the Day of ʿArafah? He said: “Yes, all of these ghusls are upon her.”

key_terms.الْأَضْحَى: Eid al-Aḍḥā, one of the occasions mentioned for ghusl
key_terms.الْفِطْرِ: Eid al-Fiṭr, one of the occasions mentioned for ghusl
key_terms.الْمَرْأَةِ: the woman being asked about in the legal ruling
key_terms.غُسْلُ: ritual bath performed for prescribed or recommended occasions
key_terms.كُلُّهُ: all of the mentioned ghusls collectively
key_terms.يَوْمِ الْجُمُعَةِ: the day of Friday, for which a ghusl is legislated
key_terms.يَوْمِ عَرَفَةَ: the Day of ʿArafah, a specified occasion for ghusl

ai.seo_question: Is a woman required to perform the ghusl of Friday, Eid al-Fiṭr, Eid al-Aḍḥā, and the Day of ʿArafah?
ai.summary: This hadith states that a woman is included in the recommended or prescribed ghusls for Friday, Eid al-Fiṭr, Eid al-Aḍḥā, and the Day of ʿArafah. It serves as a juridical text on ritual purity and worship, affirming that these ghusls apply to women as well.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1463 - Al-Halabi narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) that He said:

"I asked him about whether a woman is required to perform Ghusl (ritual purification bath) on Jumu’ah, on the day of Eid al-Fitr, on the day of Eid al-Adha, and on the day of Arafah.
Imam (as) said: 'Yes, She is required to perform all of these Ghusls.'"
